exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext log transport allows attackers to capture log data in transit via network sniffing.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted log transport mirrors the risk of data exfiltration over unencrypted protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS authentication, attackers can intercept and manipulate communications via adversary-in-the-middle attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol or Service Impersonation
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mutual TLS allows attackers to impersonate legitimate services or clients without certificate verification.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or deprecated cipher suites directly weaken the encryption protecting communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reduce Key Space
exploitedBy.relevance: Deprecated cipher suites often use reduced key spaces making them vulnerable to cryptanalytic attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Transmitted Data Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Without integrity controls, log messages in transit can be tampered with or manipulated by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Spoof Security Alerting
exploitedBy.relevance: Replaying old log messages can be used to spoof security alerts or mask current malicious activity.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Replay attacks on log streams can flood or confuse monitoring systems, effectively blocking legitimate indicators.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File Transfer Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Insecure protocol selection like UDP syslog exposes log data similar to risks from unencrypted application layer protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, log endpoints are vulnerable to flooding attacks that exhaust service resources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Traffic Duplication
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of bandwidth controls can enable attackers to duplicate and flood log traffic overwhelming the logging infrastructure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed internal routing paths can enable attackers to bridge network boundaries and access internal segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Address Translation Traversal
exploitedBy.relevance: Internal routing path exposure can facilitate NAT traversal attacks to reach otherwise inaccessible network segments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Bypassing certificate validation allows attackers to use forged or self-signed certificates to impersonate log collectors.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Certificate validation bypass in log agents enables attackers to use stolen or forged certificates without detection.
